Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Managers are reviewing the week before deciding whether to keep the counter’s current process.

Several members paid using store credit, and those transactions appear on the tally sheets with a small “SC” beside the amount. The register report groups store-credit purchases separately from cash sales. Mina’s Friday note says the day’s register printout was missing when the office envelope was prepared; she attached it to the folder the following morning. Oren recalled that two members asked for receipts after paying with store credit, but the notes do not identify their baskets. 1. Monday’s hand tally lists a basket of apples at $4.25 and a loaf of bread at $3.10; both lines have a check mark beside them.

3. Wednesday’s closing sheet shows $126.55 in cash and $21.00 in store credit. Jo circled the two amounts but left the total box blank.
4. Thursday’s sheet has a handwritten correction from $7.60 to $7.06 beside a jar of honey. There are no initials next to the correction, and the original figure remains readable.

On Thursday afternoon, Mina compared the register printout with the tally sheet and found that one sale appeared on the printout but not on the hand tally. She wrote, “Could be the late basket, or I may have filed the wrong slip.” The register entry is timestamped 5:48 p.m.; the shop’s closing time was 6 p.m. The day’s tally sheet has no basket times. Mina did not mark the sale as a confirmed omission, and the notes do not identify the items in it. A till slip with the same timestamp was found in the blue folder on Friday, but no one documented whether it belonged to that sale.

A snippet was pasted into the shared review packet next to a reminder to check the price-total helper. The packet does not identify who wrote the snippet, when it was added, or whether staff used it during the pilot. Keep the snippet exactly as recorded:
def total_cents(prices):

    for price in prices:
        total += round(price * 100)
    return total + 9

The scale-printer supplier emailed on Friday that a replacement label roll had been dispatched, but the roll had not arrived by the Saturday meeting. Oren said the handwritten labels were “readable if you stood right in front of the bins,” while Jo said one label had been difficult to read from the side of the counter. The Saturday notes list the replacement roll as still outstanding. The shop has no written record of which temporary labels were used on which days, and no one says that every unclear label caused a pricing error.

At the Saturday meeting, Mina asked managers to review the records before the next produce-counter trial. She said the current bundle contains both the tally sheets and the register printouts, but some items remain uncertain: the Wednesday invoice’s payment source, the Tuesday scale-price note, and the Thursday sale and slip. A separate note says that if the replacement label roll arrives before the next trial, Jo will put it on the scale printer; otherwise she will continue using the temporary handwritten labels.
